Fit many-facet models to ordered ratings

Source: R/api-estimation.R, R/core-cml.R, R/core-comparison-fit.R
fit_mfrm.Rd

Estimate rater severity, task or criterion difficulty, and category thresholds from a rating table. Person abilities are also returned when supported by the estimator. Supply your column names through person, facets and score; the Examples show one RSM analysis from data to results.

Usage 

fit_mfrm(
  data,
  person = NULL,
  facets = NULL,
  score = NULL,
  model = c("RSM", "PCM", "GPCM"),
  method = c("MML", "JML", "JMLE", "CML"),
  step_facet = NULL,
  slope_facet = NULL,
  rating_min = NULL,
  rating_max = NULL,
  weight = NULL,
  anchors = NULL,
  group_anchors = NULL,
  population_formula = NULL,
  person_data = NULL,
  facet_interactions = NULL,
  spec = NULL,
  control = list(),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_cml_fit'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_cml_fit'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_comparison_fit'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_comparison_fit'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

data

A data.frame in long format with one row per observed rating event. Grouped or rowwise tibbles are analyzed as one table; dplyr grouping metadata is ignored. The named model columns define the design. Pass the rating table itself, not the result of describe_mfrm_data().

person

Column name for Person identifiers (character scalar; may be supplied via spec$person).

facets

Character vector of one or more non-Person facet column names (may be supplied via spec$facets). Reserved internal names (Person, Score, Weight, score_k, theta, steps, interactions, log_slopes, beta, log_sigma2) cannot be used as facet names.

score

Column name for observed integer category scores (character scalar; may be supplied via spec$score).

model

Measurement model: "RSM" (default; shared category thresholds), "PCM" (facet-specific thresholds via step_facet), or "GPCM" (positive facet-level discriminations via slope_facet).

method

Estimator: "MML" (default marginal maximum likelihood), "JML" ("JMLE" alias; joint maximum likelihood), or "CML" (conditional maximum likelihood on Person totals for unit-weight RSM/PCM with preserved categories).

step_facet

Facet whose levels own separate step ladders in PCM and GPCM (omit for RSM; required explicitly for GPCM and CML PCM).

slope_facet

Facet whose levels own positive discriminations in GPCM (single facet name for one-family GPCM, or ordered length-two character vector for the experimental two-family MML route). Use spec$slope_reference to name the geometric-mean-one family (default: first slope facet); step_facet and noncenter_facet select their roles independently among declared non-Person facets. See fit_mfrm_technical_details.

rating_min

Optional intended minimum category score (supply together with rating_max and category_policy = "preserve" when boundary categories may be unobserved).

rating_max

Optional intended maximum category score (supply together with rating_min and category_policy = "preserve" when boundary categories may be unobserved).

weight

Optional column name of positive observation weights.

anchors

Optional direct-anchor data.frame with columns Facet, Level, and Anchor fixing logit coordinates (non-Person facets in MML; JML also permits Person anchors).

group_anchors

Optional group-mean constraint data.frame with columns Facet, Level, Group, and GroupValue.

population_formula

Optional one-sided Person-level latent-regression formula (e.g., ~ group + pretest) for unidimensional conditional-normal method = "MML".

person_data

Optional one-row-per-Person data.frame supplying covariates referenced by population_formula.

facet_interactions

Optional confirmatory two-way non-Person interaction terms (e.g., "Rater:Criterion") for RSM and PCM.

spec

Optional named list for reusing model, data and identification settings. Explicit top-level arguments override matching entries. See the specification entries in fit_mfrm_technical_details.

control

Named list of numerical and post-fit settings; for example, list(quad_points = 31, maxit = 400). Supported entries and conditions are listed in fit_mfrm_technical_details.

...

Fully named legacy flat arguments from the supported spec and control settings. Unnamed arguments, abbreviated or unknown names, and duplicate specifications across spec/control and ... fail immediately. Unused by the CML and comparison-fit summary/print methods.

object

A fitted CML result for its summary, print, covariance and log-likelihood methods, or a comparison-only result for its summary and print methods.

x

A fitted CML result for its summary, print, covariance and log-likelihood methods, or a comparison-only result for its summary and print methods.

Value

Ordinary MML/JML returns an mfrm_fit (a named list). Start with results <- summary(fit):

  • results$person_overview summarizes Person ability estimates.

  • results$facet_overview summarizes each non-Person facet.

  • results$decision reports interpretation limits and suggested actions.

Individual estimates are in fit$facets$person, fit$facets$others, fit$steps and, for GPCM, fit$slopes. Check EstimateUse or ParameterStatus for points, and CIEligible with its accompanying reason for intervals, where provided. Unavailable uncertainty is not zero. See summary.mfrm_fit() and mfrm_fit_extractors for extraction.

CML returns an mfrm_cml_fit: summary(fit)$locations and $steps contain structural estimates. Jeffreys-penalized JML returns an mfrm_jeffreys_fit (summary.mfrm_jeffreys_fit()); comparison-only fitting returns an mfrm_comparison_fit (interaction_effect_table()). These classes have different supported outputs. Full field descriptions are in fit_mfrm_technical_details.

Details

Each row represents one rating. Ordinary fitting omits rows missing required model values; review describe_mfrm_data() before fitting your own data. Repeated Person-by-facet cells are retained and flagged for review. Declaring them independent does not establish conditional independence.

Choose the intended category ladder explicitly. The default can collapse gaps in observed categories, changing the fitted steps. The example preserves a 1–4 rubric; a preserved, unobserved internal category prevents ordinary fitting.

Model and inference choices

RSM shares category thresholds; PCM gives each level of step_facet its own ladder. GPCM also estimates relative discriminations for slope_facet. The default RSM/PCM MML model fixes the Person distribution to N(0,1). Together with centered non-Person facets and steps, this fixes the overall ability-to-difficulty location as well as the population SD. These are substantive assumptions, not just a reporting scale. To estimate the mean and SD, use population_formula = ~ 1 and matching person_data (one row per Person). One-family GPCM MML estimates them by default; two-family GPCM requires different explicit settings. See fit_mfrm_technical_details for population, anchoring and slope constraints before comparing models.

MML assumes the specified population distribution. JML estimates Person and structural effects jointly; many Persons do not remove incidental-parameter bias when each has few ratings. CML conditions on Person totals and returns structural effects without Person abilities. Its supported RSM/PCM route requires unit weights and preserved categories.

Point estimates and intervals have separate availability checks. Failure to obtain an interval does not by itself invalidate an available point estimate; inspect the reported status and reason. A finite optimizer value is not automatically an interpretable estimate, and a finite SE does not establish interval coverage. mfrm_facet_intervals() documents structural intervals; fit_mfrm_technical_details gives estimator-specific conditions and references.

References

Andrich, D. (1978). A rating formulation for ordered response categories. Psychometrika, 43(4), 561–573. doi:10.1007/BF02293814

Masters, G. N. (1982). A Rasch model for partial credit scoring. Psychometrika, 47(2), 149–174. doi:10.1007/BF02296272

Muraki, E. (1992). A generalized partial credit model: Application of an EM algorithm. Applied Psychological Measurement, 16(2), 159–176. doi:10.1177/014662169201600206

Andersen, E. B. (1973). Conditional inference for multiple-choice questionnaires. British Journal of Mathematical and Statistical Psychology, 26(1), 31–44. doi:10.1111/j.2044-8317.1973.tb00504.x

Linacre, J. M. (1989). Many-Facet Rasch Measurement. MESA Press.

See also

fit_mfrm_technical_details, describe_mfrm_data(), summary.mfrm_fit(), diagnose_mfrm(), plot.mfrm_fit()

Examples 

# Load the package
library(mfrmr)

# Load example ratings and look at the first six rows
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_operational")
head(ratings)
#>                Study Person Rater    Criterion Score Group
#> 1 OperationalExample   P001   R01     Language     4     A
#> 2 OperationalExample   P001   R01 Organization     2     A
#> 3 OperationalExample   P001   R02      Content     4     A
#> 4 OperationalExample   P001   R02     Language     3     A
#> 5 OperationalExample   P001   R02 Organization     2     A
#> 6 OperationalExample   P002   R01      Content     3     A

# RSM with a preserved 1--4 rubric and fixed N(0,1) Person distribution
fit <- fit_mfrm(
  data = ratings,
  person = "Person",
  facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"),
  score = "Score",
  rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4, category_policy = "preserve",
  method = "MML",
  model = "RSM"
)

# Wright map: Person abilities, facet effects and thresholds
plot(fit)


# Save the summary, then display its tables
results <- summary(fit)
results$person_overview # One row summarizing person ability estimates
#> # A tibble: 1 × 11
#>   Persons DistributionN ReviewExcludedExtremeE…¹ EstimateUse   Mean    SD Median
#>     <int>         <int>                    <int> <chr>        <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1      48            48                        0 source_fit… -0.155 0.824 -0.208
#> # ℹ abbreviated name: ¹​ReviewExcludedExtremeEAPs
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: Min <dbl>, Max <dbl>, Span <dbl>, MeanPosteriorSD <dbl>
results$facet_overview  # One row per facet: number of levels, mean, SD, range
#> # A tibble: 2 × 7
#>   Facet     Levels MeanEstimate SDEstimate MinEstimate MaxEstimate  Span
#>   <chr>      <int>        <dbl>      <dbl>       <dbl>       <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 Criterion      3     0             0.302      -0.344       0.224 0.568
#> 2 Rater          6    -4.64e-18      0.399      -0.606       0.412 1.02 

# Check the interpretation status and recommended next step
results$decision
#>                                                           Interpretation
#> 1 Fit-readiness requirements satisfied; formal precision review required
#>   FormalInference FitReadiness
#> 1              No        ready
#>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Why
#> 1 Formal precision support has not been evaluated. These checks assess numerical readiness and the requested precision method under the specified model; they do not establish model adequacy or finite-sample coverage for this design.
#>                                                                                                                                                   NextAction
#> 1 Run `diagnose_mfrm()` and pass its result as `diagnostics =` to evaluate formal precision support; fit readiness alone is not a formal-inference decision.
